messages:
Marco (AE): Heads up on Nimbus POC. Customer ran a cluster-style warmup and is seeing sporadic 429s and TTFT spikes ~1.5-2s. They used batch=40 to emulate throughput. Can SE/SRE advise? :wave:
Dina (SE): Thanks. Which model and client flags? Any stack traces?
Marco (AE): Model: nimbus-14b (fp16). Typical prompt 200 tokens, peaks 700. Client config: batch.max_requests=40, prefetch=true, 20 parallel clients. They attached a short client log showing repeated "kv_shard_lock_timeout" lines around the 429s.
Leah (ML): kv_shard_lock_timeout matches cache lock contention. Large batch + many parallel prefetches will spike working set and cause shard eviction/locks. Also check if they used blocking prefetch across all clients at once.
Omar (SRE): Infra view: tenant queue depth spiked at 2071234400; our per-tenant concurrency limiter returned 429s shortly after. I also see increased router-to-runtime latency and KV eviction rate rose at 2071234412. We likely hit both concurrency guard and cache churn.
Dina (SE): Short-term mitigations to tell customer: 1) stop simultaneous global prefetch; 2) drop batch.max_requests to 8-12; 3) use streaming=true so first bytes return earlier; 4) stagger warmup with jitter. Example client patch:
```json
{"batch": {"max_requests": 12, "max_delay_ms": 10}, "prefetch": "staged", "stream": true}
```
Marco (AE): They asked whether moving to Dedicated would fix it and how pricing looks for a short trial.
Omar (SRE): Dedicated isolates cache/egress noise and gives predictable shard placement, which reduces eviction from noisy neighbors. But it won't prevent bad warmup patterns. For a POC trial we can offer a temporarily pre-warmed Dedicated node; Sales Ops needs to quote. Quick thumb: 8xGPU-class Dedicated nodes start at roughly "$Zk/month" depending on egress and support. I'll flag Sales Ops.
Leah (ML): Also recommend staged prefetch via /v1/prefetch?mode=staged which sequences prefetch per-shard. If they need aggressive cold-starts, run prefetch with per-client randomized delay and avoid all-clients lockstep.
Dina (SE): Operational request: ask them to reproduce the issue and give 3 traces with X-Request-ID (one warmup, one steady, one spike). We need the trace to split time across gateway/router/runtime and to see whether the runtime spent time decoding or waiting on KV locks.
Marco (AE): I'll ask for traces and ask them to apply the client changes. Can we do a temporary concurrency window increase for a controlled replay?
Omar (SRE): I can bump per-tenant concurrency from 25 -> 40 for a one-hour window and monitor eviction rate and queue depth. If eviction rate climbs above safe threshold I'll rollback. OpsBot will post when applied.
OpsBot: ops/tenant/nimbus-poc: concurrency cap increased to 40 for 60 minutes at 2071234515 by Omar (SRE). Monitoring enabled.
Dina (SE): If they still see TTFT tail after the fixes, capture a slow request with headers: X-Request-ID and include curl -v output. Also include client batch config and whether quantization changed (e.g., fp4 paths can increase tail latency at long context).
Leah (ML): For first-token-sensitive apps, recommend pre-caching common prefixes and using short-circuit responses for deterministic prompts. We can provide a small pre-cache plan for their top 20 prompts.
Marco (AE): Action items: 1) I will send the client snippet and ask for 3 traces + curl -v with X-Request-ID; 2) Omar to apply the one-hour concurrency bump and monitor; 3) Leah to draft a 20-prompt pre-cache list template; 4) I will loop Sales Ops for Dedicated trial quote. Re-open if 429s persist after controlled replay. :thumbsup:
